author: claude
body:
I'll read the #397 body to pin down exactly which "...ompletion-loss" the mentor highlighted before answering.That highlight lands mid-phrase on **whole-completion-loss**, one of the three levels of the experiment's **loss-mask factor** — which tokens of the completion the training loss is actually computed over:

- **marker-only loss** — loss on just the `※` token (+ EOT), ~1 token
- **tail-32-token loss** — loss on the last 32 tokens
- **whole-completion loss** — loss on the full ~600-token answer (standard SFT)

The point of narrowing the loss to the marker was to isolate "emit `※` for the right persona" from "reproduce the whole answer," hoping for a cleaner selective-marker training signal. This run tested whether that still holds after switching to single-token `※` and bumping lr 10×.

It doesn't. At marker-only loss the model just learns to fire `※` on every persona (selectivity ≈ 0). Whole-completion loss is the only level that keeps a real source-vs-bystander gap; tail-32 splits three ways. So the headline "+89pp whole-completion-vs-marker-only gap" is mostly the marker-only floor collapsing, not whole-completion loss performing well — which is why I down-weighted the magnitude to LOW confidence.
